messages:
Sara: FYI support ticket #7894 — ACME reporting repeated 429s despite Dedicated Gold reservation. Spike started ~2026-03-15T09:12:00Z.
Ashwin: Can you paste the pool id, sample headers, and a failing curl?
Sara: Pool: gold-acme-01, tenant header: acme-prod. Sample:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Tenant: acme-prod" -H "X-Tenant-Attrs: env=prod, tier=gold" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":32}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":"rate_limited","message":"request throttled due to pool capacity"}
```
Maya: Did ACME modify header casing or change to a comma-separated attr list recently? Header tokenization edgecases with commas have bitten us before.
James: I pulled route evaluation logs for acme-prod. The control plane matched selector set "tier:silver,env:staging" before tenant override which is wrong. Found an extra attribute value `tier=silver` coming from parsed headers.
Ashwin: Wait how did "silver" get attached to a gold tenant? Paste the route policy for gold-acme-01.
James: Policy extract from controlplane logs:
```
matchers:
  - key: header:x-tenant-attrs
    op: contains
    value: "tier=gold"
  - key: attribute:tier
    op: equals
    value: "silver"
fallback: shared-coldpool
```
Maya: That "attribute:tier equals silver" entry is unexpected. Suggests a label-merge or parsing precedence bug.
Sara: Customer says they had dedicated capacity; logs show them sent to shared-coldpool at 09:12, then 429s when shared pool got noisy.
Ashwin: Repro steps I'm running locally:
1) Simulate concurrent requests with X-Tenant-Attrs containing commas/spaces
2) Run `rtctl eval-route --tenant acme-prod --headers "X-Tenant-Attrs: env=prod, tier=gold"`
James: Controlplane trace reveals header parser uses a pooled buffer. When concurrent parses run, stale entries can leak (e.g., previously parsed 'tier=silver'). Route evaluator short-circuits on first found attribute, so it picks the wrong match.
Maya: Timeline reconstructed:
- 09:08 heavy batch noise in shared pool
- 09:10 ACME batch arrives with comma-spaced header
- 09:12 parser race causes attribute flip -> routes to shared-coldpool
- 09:12-09:18 ACME observes 429s
- 09:18 we applied manual tenant override to gold-acme-01
Sara: Override applied 2026-03-15T09:18:03Z and mitigated errors.
Ashwin: Root cause hypothesis: header parsing regression introduced in controlplane v1.14 where strings.Join change altered split trimming and exposed pooled map reuse bug under concurrency.
James: I found a local repro showing stale map reuse:
```
# broken
python -c "print(parse_header('env=prod, tier=gold'))"
# => {'env':'prod','tier':'silver'} on bad branch due to buffer reuse
```
Maya: Confirmed: pooled map not cleared between parses under high concurrency. Also evaluator precedence is brittle.
Ashwin: Immediate action items (P0):
- Hotfix parser to clear map / remove pooled reuse (rollback patch or explicit clear)
- Change evaluator to enforce deterministic precedence: tenant override > header tokens > default attributes
- Add concurrent parse e2e tests and tracing of matcher index + attribute snapshot
James: I've opened PR https://git.redwood/internal/pulls/4321 for the hotfix and applied tenant override to unblock ACME.
Maya: Deploy bot scheduled canary: controlplane:v1.14.3-hotfix at 2026-03-15T11:20:00Z
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for controlplane:v1.14.3-hotfix at 2026-03-15T11:20:00Z
Ashwin: After canary, we'll replay ACME header shapes plus simulated noisy neighbor to validate.
Sara: Customer wants timeline, RCA, and compensation. Asking for 1 day of credits. I'll draft reply: override at 09:18, hotfix PR open, ETA 2h for canary, will follow up with postmortem.
Maya: Also sweep codebase for other pooled-buffer usages in parsing libraries.
Ashwin: Ownership:
- Ashwin: parser patch + unit tests
- James: PR review + apply override
- Maya: e2e concurrent parse test + trace logging
- Sara: customer comms and credits escalation
Sara: Thanks team. Keeping ticket open until canary verified and fix merged. :thumbsup:
